name: useSpringRef
description: Create a ref for imperative animation control. Enables triggering animations without React re-renders - critical for performance in high-frequency updates like mouse tracking or gestures.

returns.description: Reference object with .start(), .set(), .stop(), .pause(), .resume() methods for controlling animations imperatively

examples.title: Basic imperative control
Mouse tracking (no re-renders)
Conditional animations
Sequencing multiple springs
Gesture with velocity
Controlling multiple values independently

methods.name: api.start(config)
methods.description: Start or update animation. Returns a Promise that resolves when animation completes.

methods.name: api.set(values)
methods.description: Immediately set spring values without animating. Useful for resetting state.

methods.name: api.stop()
methods.description: Stop all ongoing animations. Values remain at current position.

methods.name: api.pause()
methods.description: Pause animations. Can be resumed later with .resume() or .start().

methods.name: api.resume()
methods.description: Resume paused animations from current position.

keyDifferences.declarative: useSpring({ from: { x: 0 }, to: { x: 100 } }) - Animates on every React render when 'to' changes
keyDifferences.imperative: api.start({ x: 100 }) - Only animates when you explicitly call start(), no re-renders

performanceBenefits: No React re-renders - Direct spring updates bypass React reconciliation
High-frequency updates - Mouse, scroll, gesture tracking without performance penalty
Conditional control - Trigger animations based on complex logic without state changes
Sequential animations - Await animation completion before next step
Manual optimization - Full control over when and how animations trigger
commonPatterns: Mouse/touch tracking - Update springs in event handlers
Gesture animations - useDrag/useScroll with velocity and decay
Conditional animations - Trigger based on external events (WebSocket, timers)
Animation sequences - Await multiple animations in order
Performance-critical UIs - Avoid re-render overhead for smooth 60fps
importantNotes: IMPORTANT: When using ref or api, config changes in the hook definition won't auto-trigger animations. You must call api.start() explicitly.
The spring still re-renders the component when animated values change, but the trigger (api.start call) doesn't require a component re-render.
Combine with animated.to() for derived values: springs.x.to(x => `translateX(${x}px)`)
Use springs.x.get() to read current spring value synchronously
